summary: New universal conductor obstruction between normalization centres, without source CE or finite regular covers.
detailedSummary: For any excellent reduced local germ, arbitrary characteristic/residue field and all supports, a normalization fibre joining distinct local centres admits the explicit signed primary obstacle v((ce)+a^N)-N. The granted normal quantitative bound forces a negative conductor value, while actual positive conductor-primary minorants give raw value zero along a dense approaching net. Proves non-USC, no greatest C/D minorant, every-degree gap kappa=(N-nu(c))/A and perturbation gap kappa-2epsilon. USC regularization remains below the obstacle but is outside the SAME geometric D/C class. All conclusions are unverified draft mathematics relative to the qualified grant.
text:
NEW SCOPED THEOREM. Let R be any positive-dimensional excellent REDUCED local ring, with arbitrary characteristic and residue field. Let S be its finite normalization, retaining EVERY normal local centre S_i above the marked maximal ideal. For a primary gauge a put Y=disjoint union of Y_i=V_(aS_i)(S_i), X=V_a(R), and let rho:Y->X be restriction. Suppose one full fibre contains w_i in Y_i and w_j in Y_j for DISTINCT centres i!=j. Then an explicit signed PRIMARY model obstacle has a non-upper-semicontinuous raw geometric envelope, no greatest C or D minorant, and a uniform positive gap in every canonical degree. No source envelope continuity, smoothness, or finite regular cover is assumed. The normal centres may themselves be singular and nonisolated.

PROOF. Write cfrak=(R:S) and choose a regular conductor element c, granted by ENTIRE qualified G331. Every S_i is an excellent normal local DOMAIN. Choose a normalized centred support-zero divisorial valuation nu on S_i, using G331 n6's qualified full-section divisorial density. Then d=nu(c) is finite. Choose an integer N>d, N>=1.

Choose e in S that is a unit at centre i and belongs to (aS_k)^N at every other centre k. To construct it, contract those local primary ideals to S. Their maximal radicals are distinct, so they and the maximal ideal at i are pairwise comaximal. Chinese remainder gives e congruent to 1 at i and to 0 modulo every other contracted primary ideal. This also works for distinct local centres on the same global normalization component; no separating global idempotent is presumed. Since cS is contained in R, ce belongs to R. Set I=(ce)+a^N and f(v)=v(I)-N.

The conductor cannot contain a unit of R when a normalization fibre is identified: a unit conductor element would give S=R. Thus c belongs to the maximal ideal and d>0. Since nu(e)=0, nu(I)=d<N; I is proper and contains a primary power, hence is actual primary. The obstacle f is a finite continuous signed difference of primary profiles, with -N<=f<=0. Its pullback F is zero on every Y_k with k!=i: there w(e)>=N and w(c)>=0, so w(I)=N, including infinite element values. At nu, F(nu)=d-N=-b, where b=N-d>0.

The precise quantitative inequality proved inside granted G331 n6 says that for this fixed normalized divisorial nu there is a finite A>=1 such that u(nu)>=A u(w) for EVERY u in C_(S_i) and EVERY w in Y_i. Its current application meets the exact hypotheses: S_i is excellent NORMAL local domain, its completion is analytically irreducible as qualified in the grant, and aS_i is primary. The normal nonunit divisorial order bound gives nu(J)<=A w(J) for primary ideals J; units are separately zero. Uniform comparison extends this to C. Enlarging A to at least one preserves the inequality because u<=0. Taking actual decreasing limits extends it to D, with A(-infinity)=-infinity and no infinity subtraction.

If g is any target C or D minorant of f, its pullback to S_i belongs to that same granted class. Since its value at nu is at most -b, the inequality forces its value at EVERY w in Y_i to be at most -b/A=-kappa. In particular, at v_*=rho(w_i)=rho(w_j), p_R(f)(v_*)<=-kappa<0. The full conductor value at v_* is infinite because G331 makes every finite-conductor fibre a singleton.

We construct ACTUAL positive primary minorants exhibiting the opposite limiting value from centre j. Granted semilocal primary/unit gluing supplies an ideal J of S with local ideal (aS_i)^N at i and the unit ideal at every other centre. Thus q(w)=-w(J) equals -N on Y_i and zero elsewhere, and q<=F. For every r>=1 define the actual downstairs ideal B_r=cfrak J^r+a^(Nr). The first summand is contained in R because the conductor is an S-ideal contained in R; it is finitely generated as an R-ideal by Noetherianity. Its extension to S is exactly the displayed sum. Finite ideal generators and nonnegative coefficients give, on EVERY support,

rho^*(-v(B_r)/r)(w)=max{q(w)-w(cfrak)/r,-N}.

At infinite conductor value the first term is minus infinity and the second survives. On Y_i this profile is -N<=F; on every other centre it is nonpositive and below F=0. Surjectivity therefore makes it a target minorant. Its value at rho(nu) is -N, so B_r is proper; it contains a^(Nr), hence is primary. On its ACTUAL primary blowup, -E_(B_r)/r is negative effective and relatively ample, with positive degree on EVERY contracted proper integral curve BEFORE limits.

For w in Y_j of finite conductor value, these minorants tend to zero. Since all geometric competitors are nonpositive, p_R(f)(rho(w))=0 at every such point. This locus is dense in the full Y_j: the regular c is nonzero on that domain centre and has finite value at all support-zero divisorial points, and G331 n6 grants their full-section density with its Rees-DVR/dimension/historical qualifications. Choose a net of such points w_lambda->w_j. Its restrictions v_lambda tend to v_*, while p_R(f)(v_lambda)=0 and p_R(f)(v_*)<=-kappa. This is a non-USC jump of at least kappa. By own n1, greatest C and greatest D minorants do not exist.

Every actual D minorant g is USC and satisfies g(v_*)<=-kappa. Hence limsup g(v_lambda)<=-kappa, and sup_X(p_R(f)-g)>=kappa. In particular ||p_R(f)-h_m||>=kappa for EVERY canonical degree m. Bottom differences are interpreted as positive infinity. No uniform canonical convergence is possible.

Own n1's raw obstacle Lipschitz bound also proves stability without source CE. A continuous signed perturbation of size epsilon<kappa/2 has raw value at v_* at most -kappa+epsilon and values along the net at least -epsilon. It therefore retains a non-USC jump and every-minorant gap of at least kappa-2epsilon.

USC regularization cannot repair positivity. Define p^*(x)=inf_(open U containing x) sup_(z in U) p_R(f)(z). It is finite, USC and a majorant of p_R(f); continuity of f and p_R(f)<=f give p^*<=f. The zero-valued approaching net gives p^*(v_*)=0. The quantitative inequality above bounds p_R(f) by -kappa on the entire image of Y_i. The point x_0=rho(nu) has finite conductor value and belongs to no other centre image. Those other finitely many images are compact, hence closed, so a neighbourhood of x_0 meets only the image of Y_i. Thus p^*(x_0)<=-kappa. If p^* belonged to D_R, its pullback to S_i would satisfy the granted quantitative inequality, contradicting its zero value at w_i and negative value at nu. Consequently p^* is outside D_R and C_R. This is failure of positivity in the SAME independently geometric class, not a replacement cone or operator.

All mandatory G331 geometric/model/all-support/source/historical qualifications from own n1 remain attached. This proof constructs an obstacle for every identified fibre between distinct centres; it does not assume a pre-existing discrepancy of continuous source envelopes. Artifacts: n2.tex and P12.3-conductor-centre-obstruction.tex. Rerun: python delivery.py. The proof is universal mathematics relative to the qualified grant; finite artifact checks do not establish its correctness.
